subject: history
title: Revolutions: Comparison and Interpretations
welcome_lead: Today you'll stretch — compare the revolutions and weigh historians' debates.
meta_desc: GCSE History stretch — comparing revolutions, judging significance and interpretations.
final_note: You can now compare revolutions and engage with historians' arguments.

concepts.def: Wanting major, fast change to society
Wanting to keep tradition and slow change
A historian's argued view, backed by evidence

walkthroughs.body_html:
All three revolutions overthrew an old regime.

Each had financial crisis, war strain and rising new ideas — Enlightenment thought for America and France, Marxism for Russia. All built new constitutions or systems.

The American revolution kept private property and built a stable republic.

The French revolution turned radical with the Reign of Terror, then military dictatorship under Napoleon. The Russian revolution went furthest left — abolishing private business and creating a one-party communist state.

Some historians stress big ideas — Enlightenment, Marxism.

Others stress economic crisis or the role of leaders like Lenin or Robespierre. Revisionist historians focus on women and ordinary people — the sans-culottes, the soviets. A strong essay weighs these views with evidence.
